speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: There has not been a pick-up in property-related foreclosures thus far.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The first is in relation to what the Minister of State replied earlier in terms of the data.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I refer to the Ministry of Law's (MinLaw's) data recently, which highlighted the number of mortgagee listings jumped in the first quarter of 2023, with more distress sales expected in the second half of the year as bankruptcy applications increased – I think this from a Business Times article in relation to the MinLaw data.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: That was the first supplementary question in relation to what the Minister of State had shared.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Can the Minister of State reconcile that MinLaw data for the first quarter?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The second is in relation to my concern about the high interest rates and increase in the mortgagee-listing statistics.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: For some households, a $240-on-average increase in mortgage payments can be quite substantial.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Can the Minister of State share whether there are any further updates on the household debt situation in Singapore at the current situation and also going forward as well?

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: I will address the household debt situation question first, in reference to the written Parliamentary Question that MAS answered yesterday.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: First is that households with outstanding mortgages will naturally see higher borrowing costs as interest rates rise from the exceptionally low levels in the past decade, so they will face the impact of a rise at different points of time, depending on the types of loan packages that they have taken up.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: So, 2% for increase in mortgage payments versus a 10% increase of monthly income over the last three years.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: While we understand and empathise that there are raises in how much mortgage layouts there are, this comparison between 10% increase in money income as well as 2% increase in mortgage would have helped cushion the increase in mortgage payments.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: The other point here is also, maybe to give the Members some more updated information and details on borrowers who refinanced between August 2022 and February 2023.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: They would have faced a larger mortgage payment increase given the sharper increases in interest rates during that period.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Again, if you take it on as a whole, the average increase in monthly income or those who had refinance in the past 12 months was about 10% over the last three years.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: It would have, to some degree, helped to cushion the increase in their mortgage payments.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: MAS estimated that the income increase over the last three years was because most of its borrowers had secured a new loan or refinanced that existing loan three years ago.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: The use of mortgagee listings as an indicator of households and businesses in distress may be limited.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: The extent of distressed sales could be or likely be overstated, in part due to double counting.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: We are not privy to the auction houses' methodologies, but there are challenges in tracking such listings as there is no central database.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: For example, a property that is put up for sale may count as several listings at the bank or the owner listing it with multiple agencies.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: The Member mentioned the recent media report last month that suggested that there is a spike in distressed property listings in its headline.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: This sharp increase referred to a quarter-on-quarter change from Q4 of 2022, which may reflect a low-based effect from the muted market activity in the year-end period.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: And now with higher rates and increasing uncertainty over global growth prospects, MAS continues to urge all borrowers to exercise caution and to ensure that you are able to service your debts when taking on long-term financial commitments, including big ticket items such as property purchases.
